title: Regression trees: splits, leaves and predictions

items.stem: A regression tree is deciding how to split a node. Which split does it choose?

options.text: The split that puts the same number of training rows on each side
The split that most reduces the total squared error of the targets in the two child nodes
The split after which a straight line fits the targets on each side most closely
The split at the median of the feature most correlated with the target

items.stem: A leaf of a regression tree holds four training houses with prices of 210, 240, 250 and 260 thousand dollars. A new house lands in this leaf. What price does the tree predict?
In one or two sentences, explain why a regression tree grown until every leaf holds a single training row tends to predict new data poorly.
A regression tree is trained on houses from 1,000 to 3,000 square feet, and prices rise steadily with size. What does it predict for a 5,000-square-foot house?

options.text: A price above any training price, continuing the upward trend in the data
The same price it predicts for the largest houses in the training data
No prediction, because the input is outside the range it was trained on
The average price of all the houses in the training data
